intent: New concept art refining Pixel Pod to two main shell halves plus battery hatch
status: Concept only, not verified CAD or STL
common_prompt:
Use case: product-mockup. Create polished industrial-design concept art of SIMPLIFIED PIXEL POD, a fun student-built FDM printed virtual-pet handheld. Image 1 is ONLY aesthetic reference: retain friendly green/cream/yellow retro identity, but discard its old rear switch, front IR lenses and decorative multipart borders. Image 2 is the real FULL MAIN BOARD layout reference, 96 mm wide by 105 mm tall. Image 3 is the real 50x50 mm POWER BOARD reference. Electronics geometry reference takes precedence over image 1.
USER'S SIMPLIFICATION: exactly TWO main shell halves: a single cream FRONT SHELL and a single deep green REAR SHELL. ONE small separate rear BATTERY HATCH for access without splitting main halves. No separate side skins, corner caps, external frame, external armor, separate facade, decorative extra panels, giant assemblies of tiles, or spare outer shells. Button caps, a small RGB collar and necessary internal insulating battery shelf are small functional parts, not additional shell halves. Broad flat front/back surfaces, softened rounded rectangular outline, short chamfered edge transitions rather than bulbous compound curves. Face-down printable major faces and accessible screw assembly, no claims of invisible as-printed layer lines. Attractive satin finish target, not deep fake woodgrain/ridges or shiny injection molding.
Exact controls below small upper-center landscape screen: FOUR individual DIRECTION buttons in a diamond on left, FOUR action buttons in a diamond on right (X top, Y left, A right, B bottom), ONE central MODE slightly lower. Exactly NINE buttons. LCD uses existing 280x240 landscape proportions, active width roughly a third of device width; cheerful COLOR pixel pet, not a new giant display. ONE RGB round light upper right beside display. Keep substantial depth for tall socketed components. Do not shrink the electronics to sell a thin case.
CRITICAL IR CHANGE: ONE rectangular recessed OPEN WINDOW on the actual horizontal TOP EDGE near left (as seen from front) exposes exactly two outward-pointing optical components: IR TX and IR RX. NO optics on the front face, no camera-like pair above screen on front. Top view must visibly show the aperture on the horizontal top surface. No opaque tinted plastic presumed IR transparent.
FRONT CONTENTS: the FULL 96x105 main board, extending continuously behind BOTH the screen AND all nine switches, mounts to supports inside the front shell. Never replace main PCB with a screen-sized board. Support PCB at mount holes, don't clamp LCD glass. ESP32/socket and other components occupy the rear side of that main PCB too. Do not invent a second small controller board attached to the LCD.
REAR CONTENTS: power board and battery STACK IN DEPTH in the LOWER rear shell, not side-by-side and not in the plane of the main board. From the front toward the rear hatch the order is: full main assembly, clearance, 50x50 power PCB on its own supports, air clearance + insulated separator/battery pocket, removable battery, rear hatch. Battery and power board overlap in plan view, but do NOT touch. Keep whole top-center rear zone free of battery/power/metal for antenna. Battery is an unbranded placeholder labeled BATTERY SIZE TBD, non-compressed in a pocket with pull tab and reachable wire connector; battery can be accessed alone by removing the small hatch while main shells remain joined. A captive screw secures hatch; no battery pressing onto PCB or component pins. Internal rails/retainers act on the supporting tray, not on soft battery pouch. Wiring space, screw bosses, small speaker and motor retention room remain to be validated, don't fill every cubic millimeter with battery.
POWER PORTS ARE TIED TO PCB: power PCB rotated 180deg in its plane relative to image3, component side facing rear, in lower rear region with its side switch near shell side. In a straight rear view switch is LEFT near bottom and USB-C faces BOTTOM; in a front view switch is on user's RIGHT near bottom. Adjacent edges of same PCB; never put switch on rear face. No remote switch wiring, no second USB. USB and switch stay aligned to actual board's fixed relative geometry. Board/hatch alignment and physical fit are provisional.
Only short title and simple labels if needed. White studio background, cohesive consistent views, realistic volumes. Footer exactly CONCEPT ONLY - FIT CHECK REQUIRED. Do NOT claim printable files, exact fit, real verified internals, support-free printing, tested safety or factory readiness.

variants.prompt: Asset: clean exterior concept sheet, title PIXEL POD - SIMPLE SHELL. Show one LARGE front/top/right three-quarter hero of fully assembled device clearly revealing the top-surface IR window and side switch; a smaller rear three-quarter view showing ONE small lower rear battery hatch with pull recess and captive screw; and small top view showing IR TX/RX opening only on top edge. Include one small rear view with ONLY battery hatch removed, exposing battery pull tab but not power circuitry because insulated pocket separates it. No exploded components or alternative designs on this sheet. Keep exterior uncomplicated, simple cream front and green back, green direction/action caps, yellow mode and small RGB collar. Outer halves have one clean perimeter seam and four recessed rear screws; battery hatch is the only other rear panel. No front IR pair. No decorative extra panel around screen. The finished body remains near-square portrait, not long rectangular like a phone.

Asset: companion simplified assembly concept sheet, title PIXEL POD - INSIDE. One moderately exploded three-quarter product illustration showing cream front shell, FULL rectangular main PCB with screen and all nine switches mounted on it, green rear shell with internal power-board support and insulating battery shelf, battery nearer the rear exterior and ONE small hatch. Keep only two large shell halves and one small hatch; avoid exploded decorative scraps. A small assembled front/top thumbnail establishes same simple Pixel Pod and TOP EDGE IR window. A small side cutaway inset MUST clearly show front-to-back depth order labeled MAIN BOARD, POWER BOARD, INSULATED POCKET, BATTERY, HATCH. Power board and battery overlap one BEHIND the other in lower rear, never side-by-side in rear view. Use schematic plain board surfaces based on the reference outline/layout rather than invented hyperdetailed chips; label ILLUSTRATIVE INTERNALS. Main board FULL height behind screen and all buttons, no ribbon dangling from LCD to imaginary tiny PCB. Show ample separation, not physical battery contact with electronics. Show a hand-free battery pull tab access detail with hatch removed and power board remaining installed beneath insulated pocket. Limit text to clear functional labels: FRONT SHELL, MAIN BOARD + SCREEN, REAR SHELL, POWER BOARD, INSULATED BATTERY POCKET, BATTERY SIZE TBD, BATTERY HATCH. No assembly certification or unsupported dimensions.
